description: Figure 2 is a pie chart illustrating the original distribution of five emotion categories within the IEMOCAP dataset, with percentages shown relative to the total number of utterances. The chart is divided into five distinct slices, each representing one emotion category: neutral, frustration, sadness, anger, and happiness. The slice corresponding to “neutral” emotion is the largest, colored dark gray, and accounts for approximately 30% of the utterances. The “frustration” slice, colored light gray, is the second largest, representing about 25%. The “sadness” slice, in blue, is the third largest at roughly 20%. The “anger” slice, in green, is smaller at approximately 15%. The smallest slice, “happiness,” colored red, represents about 10% of the utterances. The chart includes a legend that matches each emotion label to its respective color, and the percentage values are displayed directly within each slice. The slices are arranged in descending order of size, starting from the top left and moving clockwise.
